title: The Lost Shift
lead: Forty miners went down Tube Nineteen nine weeks ago, and they were written off the same day. Yesterday someone on Shift Row heard knocking on the old ore pipe: three knocks, a pause, three knocks. Ulla Greaves has a rope, a bad temper and no way past the collapse, and her eldest son's name is on that list.
anyone: Forty miners went down Tube Nineteen nine weeks ago, and they were written off the same day. Yesterday someone on Shift Row heard knocking on the old ore pipe: three knocks, a pause, three knocks. Ulla Greaves has a rope, a bad temper and no way past the collapse, and her eldest son's name is on that list.

gm.truth: Twenty-nine of them are alive, and they've been alive for nine weeks because of the very things they were taught to fear. Slag crawlers eat heat. They only attack what's hot. The trapped miners, under a stubborn old powder hand named Nerys Okoro, with Ulla's son Joren keeping the tally, learned to cool their suits, walk slowly and live among them. The crawlers shed a dense, oily scale, and the miners have been burning it for light. It burns hotter and cleaner than anything the Stack makes: weight for weight, about a third better than refined fuel. So the most valuable thing on the moon has been eating miners for a hundred years, and nobody ever noticed because they kept killing them on sight. Nerys and the others know exactly what they've got, and they've talked it over for nine weeks. The knocking isn't a call for help. It's a warning to stay out, in the old shift code for gas. Ulla reads that code better than anyone alive, and she's chosen to hear it wrong. They don't want to be rescued. If anyone finds out, every power in known space will come to harvest the crawlers. Deeper in, behind a wall the crawlers won't touch, is what a coughing old surveyor has sworn to for years: a sealed Concord strategic reserve, lost in the paperwork a century ago. Getting that out would take miners and managers working side by side, and it's the GM's choice how much of it to reveal here.
beats: The shaft. Ulla, the crew and a pipe that knocks. An old woman in the crowd frowns at the rhythm and says that's not the code she'd use for help, and Ulla tells her to shut her mouth, too quickly.
Getting past the collapse: a crawl through old tubes, heat shimmer, and something big and pale shifting in the dark. A careful captain will notice the claw marks stop just short of anything cold.

The camp. Lamps burning with a strange white flame, thin but healthy people, and Nerys Okoro, who isn't even slightly glad to see them. A crawler the size of a shuttle slides past, and nobody looks up.

Ulla and her son. He's alive, and he's the one who used to read her everything, and he won't come up. Dr. Aduro's medic has one look and says these people are in better shape than the ones on Shift Row. Everyone is looking at the lamp.
The fuel gauge back on the Meridian, and a choice about what to do with what the captain now knows.
routes: Dig through: engineering and athletics to clear the collapse, or survival to take the long way through the Tubes without a suit heater.
Understand it: science and awareness to work out why the crawlers ignore the camp, and what the scale really is.
Win them over: persuasion and medicine, offering real care for the twenty-nine and an honest promise about what the fleet will and won't do with the secret.
checks: survival:moderate to cross the Tubes with your suit run cold
athletics:moderate to squeeze and climb through the collapse
science:hard to work out what the crawlers shed and why it burns
awareness:easy to see that the claw marks stop at the cold rock
persuasion:hard to get Nerys Okoro to trust a uniform
medicine:easy to see that the survivors are healthier than they should be
fights: cinder_wyrm if someone comes in hot, and they usually do. Shutting down heaters and standing very still makes it lose interest.
outcomes: If the secret is kept with a small, careful harvest, the fleet gets a slow and steady private fuel supply, and twenty-nine people who'll guard it. Secrets like that have a lifespan.
If the captain tells the whole colony, Cinder Reach becomes rich, and within months every faction with a ship is at the door, hungry and armed. Crawlers start dying in large numbers.

If the captain leaves them alone and tells no one, the miners stay in the dark with their strange neighbors. The fleet stays short of fuel, and Nerys Okoro sends a lamp, with one note, which Joren wrote, and which someone has to read to Ulla.
If the fleet takes everything it can, the fuel problem eases for months, and the survivors, Ulla and the crawlers all pay for it. Later, the tubes that the crawlers kept open start to plug.

If miners and managers are brought together to open the reserve, the fleet's fuel worries end for a long time, and it takes a miracle of cooperation between people who've sworn to kill each other. Rennick knows where the old survey maps are.
gm.rewards: A private supply of about one refined_fuel per visit if the deal is honest, a survivor's knowledge that helps in What Happens If It Stops, and Ulla's lifelong debt for finding her son.
